source: Clark, Tafjord, Richardson (2020) Transformers as Soft Reasoners over Language
finding: A fine-tuned transformer (RuleTaker) learned to answer true/false questions over facts and rules written in English. It transfers to deeper chains than it saw in training.
numbers: About 99% accuracy in-distribution; 95%+ on test data needing deeper chaining than training; also transfers to two hand-authored rulebases and to paraphrased rules.
limits: Fine-tuned on synthetic data, simple closed-world rules. Later work (FOLIO, c12) shows this does not carry over to rich natural-language FOL.
agent_relevance: Rule following over text is learnable, but as a trained skill. It is not a guarantee for a prompted agent.

source: Tafjord, Dalvi, Clark (2021) ProofWriter: Generating Implications, Proofs, and Abductive Statements over Natural Language
finding: A generative model iterates a one-step implication generator to produce proofs that reflect actual decisions, not after-the-fact stories.
numbers: Proof accuracy on RuleTaker +9% absolute over earlier methods; generalizes to unseen proof depths and out-of-domain sets; can do abduction (name a missing fact) with high precision.
limits: Synthetic rule data; a trained model, not a prompt.
agent_relevance: Design hint for S4/S8: have the model emit one inference step at a time and check each step, not one long free chain.

source: Saparov, He (2023) Language Models are Greedy Reasoners: A Systematic Formal Analysis of Chain-of-Thought (ICLR)
finding: Parsed GPT-3 chains of thought into formal proofs. Single deduction steps are mostly valid, even in fictional worlds. The weakness is proof planning: when several valid steps exist, the model takes misleading ones and does not search.
numbers: text-davinci-002 only; 400 examples per condition, 48 conditions, Wilson 95% CI. Only the largest model beat chance (350M, 1.3B, 6.7B did not). 1- and 3-hop fine; 5-hop top-down fell to chance. True ontology (real facts) much better and did not drop from 3 to 5 hops; fictional and false ontologies were similar to each other.
quote: LLMs are quite capable of making correct individual deduction steps
limits: Old model family (2022). Label accuracy correlates poorly with strict proof accuracy, so answer accuracy can hide bad reasoning. Modus ponens only.
agent_relevance: Supports G2/G3: check each step by code and do not trust the final label. The model leans on world knowledge to skip hops, a risk when testing a rule set that mixes real and invented facts.

source: Saparov, Pang, Padmakumar, Joshi, Kazemi, Kim, He (2023) Testing the General Deductive Reasoning Capacity of LLMs Using OOD Examples (NeurIPS)
finding: Tested 4 LLMs (GPT and PaLM families, FLAN-T5) on many deduction rules, not only modus ponens, asking them to generalize to deeper, wider and compositional proofs from simple demonstrations.
numbers: Chain of thought generalizes to compositional proofs. Models struggle to generalize to longer proofs. They do not produce hypothetical subproofs (proof by cases, proof by contradiction) without explicit demonstrations of those rules.
limits: Synthetic programmable dataset; models from 2023. Exact per-model percentages were in figures, not read.
agent_relevance: Boundary for any prompt-built logic check: reductio and case-split reasoning need worked examples in the prompt, or must move into a solver.

source: Pan, Albalak, Wang, Wang (2023) Logic-LM: Empowering LLMs with Symbolic Solvers for Faithful Logical Reasoning (EMNLP Findings)
finding: LLM translates the problem to symbolic form (LP, FOL, CSP, SAT) and an external solver (Pyke, Prover9, python-constraint, Z3) answers. Beats standard and CoT prompting on all 5 datasets. Falls back to CoT when the formula does not run.
numbers: GPT-4 accuracy Standard / CoT / Logic-LM: PrOntoQA 77.40/98.79/83.20; ProofWriter 52.67/68.11/79.66; FOLIO 69.11/70.58/78.92; LogicalDeduction 71.33/75.25/87.63; AR-LSAT 33.33/35.06/43.04. GPT-3.5 (chat) FOLIO 45.09/57.35/62.74. Average gain over standard 39.2% and over CoT 18.4% (GPT-3.5); GPT-4 +24.98% and +10.44%.
limits: On PrOntoQA, GPT-4 CoT (98.79) beats Logic-LM (83.20): when the chain is simple forward modus ponens, the solver route loses. CoT gain on FOLIO is small (+11.75%) and negative on AR-LSAT (-3.2%).
agent_relevance: Core evidence for a solver in S4/S8: translate, then let code decide. Keep a fallback and measure translation separately.

source: Pan et al. (2023) Logic-LM: executable rate and self-refinement (Table 3)
finding: Share of generated formulas that run, and the effect of feeding the solver error message back for repair.
numbers: Executable rate before to after refinement, GPT-4: FOLIO 79.9% to 85.8%; ProofWriter 99.0% flat; AR-LSAT 32.6% to 39.8%. GPT-3.5: FOLIO 66.7% to 84.3%; ProofWriter 87.3% to 95.6%; AR-LSAT 11.3% to 21.8%. Accuracy among executable FOLIO items with GPT-4: 80.4 before, 79.9 after.
limits: Refinement fixes syntax, not meaning: accuracy among executable problems barely moves. Diminishing returns after several rounds.
agent_relevance: Revision from real solver output works for syntax (matches G2). It does not catch a wrong translation that still runs (see c11, c16).

source: Ye, Chen, Dillig, Durrett (2023) SatLM: Satisfiability-Aided Language Models Using Declarative Prompting (NeurIPS)
finding: LLM writes a declarative spec of constraints and an SMT/SAT solver (Z3) finds the answer, instead of writing an imperative program. Better on constraint and logic problems.
numbers: code-davinci-002 greedy, Standard/CoT/ProgLM/SatLM: GSM-Sys 21.0/46.5/43.4/69.4; LSAT 22.0/23.5/-/35.0; BoardgameQA 44.6/60.7/-/79.4; CLUTRR 41.2/40.8/58.9/68.3; ProofWriter 76.6/80.1/83.7/99.7. SatLM beats ProgLM with p<0.05 (bootstrap) except GSM greedy, where equal.
limits: Without the solver (SatNoSolver) accuracy falls to about the standard-prompt level. In 40 manual cases most CoT-solver failures are planning errors (72.5% on GSM-Sys).
agent_relevance: The benefit comes from the solver, not the declarative prompt alone. Planning errors dominate when there is no solver.

source: Ye et al. (2023) SatLM: abstention on UNSAT and AMBIG (Table 5)
finding: The solver can return UNSAT (contradictory spec) or AMBIG (under-determined spec). These signals let the system abstain from likely wrong answers.
numbers: Selective accuracy on GSM-Sys 77% for SatLM vs 45% for ProgLM, with lower coverage. SatLM coverage is lower on all three datasets, yet overall accuracy is higher on GSM-Sys and CLUTRR.
limits: Abstaining costs coverage.
agent_relevance: Direct fit to S4: UNSAT means the stated rules contradict; AMBIG means a premise is missing. Both are free, code-checked doubt signals (G1).

source: Olausson, Gu, Lipkin, Zhang, Solar-Lezama, Tenenbaum, Levy (2023) LINC: Logical Inference via Neurosymbolic Computation (EMNLP)
finding: LLM acts as a semantic parser to FOL, Prover9 decides, 10-way majority vote over samples. Compared with naive, scratchpad and CoT prompting for StarCoder+, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.
numbers: FOLIO (182 examples): LINC gains for StarCoder+ and GPT-3.5, but GPT-4 LINC is below GPT-4 CoT, difference not significant (McNemar p=0.58). ProofWriter balanced subset: LINC GPT-3.5 96.4%, GPT-4 98.3%, near ceiling at every proof depth; GPT-3.5 baselines fall to chance beyond depth 1. FOL syntax errors: 38% StarCoder+, 24% GPT-3.5, 13% GPT-4.
limits: Failure modes: L1 missing implicit facts (e.g. Person(Harry)), L2 FOL cannot express the content, L3 syntax errors (same symbol used with different arity).
agent_relevance: Boundary: on messy natural text a strong model's own reasoning can match the solver route. Gains are largest on long synthetic rule sets.

source: Olausson et al. (2023) LINC: GPT-4 error analysis on FOLIO
finding: Compared where GPT-4+LINC and GPT-4+CoT fail. LINC fails by losing information in translation (e.g. merging facts into one symbol). CoT fails by invalid deductions.
numbers: Fault types L1-L3 for LINC and C2 (invalid deduction) for CoT; the error sets differ, so the two routes are partly complementary.
limits: One dataset, 182 items.
agent_relevance: Run the solver route and the plain route as separate views and compare in code (G4: agreement is a hint, not proof).

source: Han et al. (2022/2024) FOLIO: Natural Language Reasoning with First-Order Logic (EMNLP 2024)
finding: Human-written benchmark: 1,430 conclusions over 487 premise sets, each with FOL annotations verified by an inference engine. Also an NL-to-FOL translation set.
numbers: Test labels 87 true / 78 false / 61 unknown (majority baseline 38.5%). Fine-tuned: BERT-base 56.8, Flan-T5-large 65.7 best. Few-shot NL: LLaMA-13B 33.6, LLaMA-70B 44.0, text-davinci-002 49.5, GPT-3.5 58.3, GPT-4 about 69. CoT +4% over GPT-4 few-shot, self-consistency +0.6% more, LINC about +9%, Logic-LM and DetermLR more than +13%.
limits: Subset HybLogic (deeper chains) leaves GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 only slightly above chance, while WikiLogic is easier. Some table cells were garbled in the PDF text; values here come from the running text.
agent_relevance: Use FOLIO-style items as test cases for the verify state. The FOL annotations let code check a rule set for consistency.

source: Han et al. (2024) FOLIO: NL to FOL translation (Table 5, Table 6)
finding: Models write syntactically valid FOL but often not the right FOL. Validity is high; semantic match to the gold is low.
numbers: Syntactic validity: GPT-3.5 68.4 zero-shot, 93.3 few-shot; GPT-4 86.1, 93.9. Inference-engine execution accuracy (the formula gives the right label): GPT-3.5 50.4 zero-shot, 56.0 few-shot; GPT-4 51.7, 63.8. By subset (WikiLogic vs HybLogic) execution accuracy: GPT-3.5 68.88 vs 47.70; GPT-4 75.43 vs 53.10.
limits: Execution accuracy is an indirect measure of translation quality.
agent_relevance: A formula that parses is not a formula that is right. Solver acceptance is not proof of faithful translation (G3).

source: Qi, Ma, Li, Du, Hui, Wu, Laili, He (2025) Large Language Models Meet Symbolic Provers for Logical Reasoning Evaluation (ProverQA, ICLR)
finding: ProverGen: an LLM writes natural language and a prover checks it, giving 1,500 FOL problems (easy 1-2 steps, medium 3-5, hard 6-9) with reasoning chains, distractors and shuffled premises.
numbers: CoT accuracy easy/medium/hard: GPT-4o 94.2/79.4/50.0; Claude-3.5-Sonnet 95.2/83.6/56.4; Mistral-Large 92.6/75.8/52.2; Llama3.1-70B 90.4/73.2/46.8. Standard prompting GPT-4o 87.2/68.6/46.2. Other sets, CoT GPT-4o: ProntoQA 100, ProofWriter 67.3, FOLIO 72.1. Mean CoT gain over standard: easy +12.86, medium +8.43, hard +3.86.
limits: 2024 chat models; no reasoning models tested. CoT helps little on hard items, so chain length is not the only bottleneck.
agent_relevance: Hard multi-step FOL is still near 50% for strong chat models. This is where a solver pays most.

source: Qi et al. (2025) ProverQA: distractor and premise-order ablation, finetuning
finding: Removing distractors helps; ordering premises along the proof helps more. Finetuning Llama3.1-8B on ProverQA training data transfers to other sets.
numbers: GPT-4o CoT easy/medium/hard: default 94.2/79.4/50.0; no distractors 94.4/82.2/57.4; no distractors and ordered premises 95.6/87.4/62.4. Finetuning gain on ProverQA: +21.4 easy, +44.0 medium, +34.6 hard points.
limits: Finetuned model is 8B; finetuning on FOLIO alone lowered some other sets (e.g. ProverQA easy -22.4 relative to one baseline in the table).
agent_relevance: Premise order and irrelevant premises move accuracy by up to 12 points. A scaffold that selects and orders relevant premises in code should help.

source: Xu, Fei, Pan, Liu, Lee, Hsu (2024) Faithful Logical Reasoning via Symbolic Chain-of-Thought (SymbCoT, ACL)
finding: Fully LLM-based: translate to symbolic form, plan and solve with logic rules, then a verifier checks both translation and chain. No external solver.
numbers: Gains over Naive/CoT/Logic-LM averaged over 5 datasets: +21.56/+6.11/+3.53 (GPT-3.5) and +22.08/+9.31/+7.88 (GPT-4). Constraint-optimisation form (GPT-4): +13.32 over CoT, +3.12 over Logic-LM. GPT-3.5 on FOLIO did not beat Logic-LM.
limits: The verifier is the same LLM, so its checks are not independent (G4). Per-cell tables were garbled; only summary gains used.
agent_relevance: A prompt-only translate-plan-solve-verify loop works, but its check is weaker than a real solver.

source: Kirtania, Gupta, Radhakrishna (2024) Logic-LM++: Multi-Step Refinement for Symbolic Formulations
finding: Repair of the symbolic translation often fixes syntax but adds meaning errors (e.g. 'No young person teaches' turned into 'All young people teach'). Fix: propose several refinements, have the LLM compare them pairwise, keep the better.
numbers: GPT-4, Logic-LM to Logic-LM++: FOLIO 78.92 to 84.80; ProofWriter 79.66 to 79.66; AR-LSAT 43.04 to 46.32. GPT-3.5: FOLIO 62.80 to 62.25; ProofWriter 58.33 to 58.83; AR-LSAT 26.41 to 28.13. Average gain 5% over Logic-LM.
limits: Pairwise judging uses the same model family. The gain is clear only for GPT-4 on FOLIO; flat or noisy elsewhere.
agent_relevance: Semantic drift under repair is a known hazard. Keep both versions and let code compare them on held-out checks.

source: Calanzone, Teso, Vergari (2024) Logically Consistent Language Models via Neuro-Symbolic Integration
finding: Fine-tune with a semantic loss over implication and negation constraints so a model does not contradict a knowledge base or itself. Reports LLaMa-2 70b answering true to both a statement and its negation.
numbers: Trained on BeliefBank splits. Plain supervised fine-tuning does not fix consistency (about 10% true vs 90% false facts, so the model says false to everything). The neuro-symbolic loss improves factuality and consistency over Macaw-Large and ConCoRD; test time 2405 s vs 3669 s for ConCoRD.
limits: Small models (Macaw-Large, LLaMa-2 7B), simple constraints. Consistency gains do not always carry to other data (the paper says so).
agent_relevance: Names a property we want: no contradictions across stated rules. A prompt-time version is to ask p and not-p separately and compare in code.

source: Parmar, Patel, Varshney, Nakamura, Luo, Mashetty, Mitra, Baral (2024) LogicBench: Systematic Evaluation of Logical Reasoning Ability of LLMs (ACL)
finding: 25 reasoning patterns in propositional, first-order and non-monotonic logic, each testing one inference rule. Tests GPT-4, ChatGPT, Gemini-Pro, Llama-2-7B, Mistral-7B with CoT.
numbers: Binary QA, propositional logic, average over rules: Llama-2 57.9, Mistral 58.8, ChatGPT 81.9, Gemini 88.8, GPT-4 89.6. GPT-4 per rule: hypothetical syllogism 100, destructive dilemma 88.3, modus tollens 76.7, material implication 73.3. First-order disjunctive syllogism: GPT-4 95, ChatGPT 78.3, Llama 43.3. Weakest rules involve negation.
limits: Single-rule items, short text. Table columns were read from PDF text and could be shifted by a column in places.
agent_relevance: Negation inside rules is the main failure. Put a negation-flip test (ask p, then not-p) into S4.

source: Parmar et al. (2024) LogicBench: rule-type dependence and human check
finding: Models sometimes ignore context needed for the conclusion. GPT-4 is about 85% on hypothetical syllogism but about 59% (Yes-class accuracy) on modus tollens in the analysis section. Bigger models do better.
numbers: Yes-class accuracy: GPT-4 about 85% (HS) vs about 59% (MT). Human check on 50 items across the 25 patterns: roughly 83-88% depending on task.
limits: Human sample small (50 items, 3 annotators). The 59% and the table's 76.7 for MT differ by metric (Yes-class vs overall); do not mix them.
agent_relevance: Modus tollens (deny the consequent) is a good probe of whether the model checks for contradiction rather than only chaining forward.

source: Patel et al. (2024) Multi-LogiEval: Evaluating Multi-Step Logical Reasoning Ability of LLMs (EMNLP)
finding: Multi-step logic with more than 30 inference rules, depth 1 to 5, propositional, first-order and non-monotonic. Zero-shot CoT on GPT-4, ChatGPT, Gemini-Pro, Yi-34B, Orca-2-13B, Mistral-7B.
numbers: Average accuracy about 68% at depth 1 down to about 43% at depth 5. Sample counts by depth 410, 442, 310, 280, 110.
limits: Context generated with Claude-2 plus checks; yes/no items only.
agent_relevance: Each added inference step costs accuracy, so split proofs into small, individually checked steps.

source: Lampinen, Dasgupta, Chan et al. (2024) Language models, like humans, show content effects on reasoning tasks (PNAS Nexus; arXiv 2207.07051)
finding: Compared Chinchilla, PaLM 2, Flan-PaLM 2 and GPT-3.5 with human participants on natural language inference, syllogism validity and the Wason task. Both show belief bias: accuracy is higher when content supports the logical answer.
numbers: Past human work: people call a believable invalid syllogism valid about 90% of the time. Wason: significant realistic-over-arbitrary advantage in humans, Chinchilla, PaLM 2-L, GPT-3.5 (all z>2.2, p<0.03); marginal in PaLM 2-M and Flan-PaLM 2 (p about 0.08). Human participants were not above chance overall on the Wason task. NLI: little content effect.
limits: Online human participants; 2022-2023 model families. Some models do better with nonsense than arbitrary nouns on the Wason task.
agent_relevance: A plausible-sounding contradiction will be accepted. Rename predicates to neutral symbols before any logic check.

source: Lyu, Havaldar, Stein, Zhang, Rao, Wong, Apidianaki, Callison-Burch (2023) Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
finding: Two stages: the LM translates the question into a symbolic chain (Python, Datalog, PDDL), and a deterministic solver runs it. The chain is then a faithful record of how the answer was reached.
numbers: Beats standard CoT on 9 of 10 benchmarks across 4 domains; relative gain 6.3% on math word problems, 3.4% on planning, 5.5% on multi-hop QA.
limits: Faithful to the symbolic chain, not a check that the translation is right.
agent_relevance: Same split as our schema: the model fills a slot, the program decides.

source: Feng, Xu, Hao, Shen, Chen (2023) Language Models can be Logical Solvers (LoGiPT)
finding: Fine-tune an LLM to imitate the solver's reasoning trace, so there is no parse failure and no external call. Motivated by parse failure: Vicuna-13B gives executable formulas on only 17% of ProofWriter.
numbers: Parse success: Vicuna-13B 17.0% ProofWriter / 40.8% PrOntoQA; CodeLlama-13B-Base 0.33% / 0.4%; CodeLlama-13B-Instruct 71.3% / 77.8%. LoGiPT 13B about 81-90% on ProofWriter and about 96% on PrOntoQA, versus GPT-4 CoT 68.1 / 98.8 and Logic-LM GPT-4 79.7 / 83.2.
limits: Needs solver-trace fine-tuning data; not available in a prompt-only scaffold. Which LoGiPT variant scored which cell was not clear from the PDF text.
agent_relevance: Small open models are poor translators; a scaffold on a small model should expect most formulas to fail.

source: Liu, Xu, Wang et al. (2024) Logic-of-Thought: Injecting Logic into Contexts for Full Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Extract propositions, expand them with logical laws (transitivity, contraposition), turn them back into text and add them to the prompt. Avoids the information loss when a solver sees only the translated formula.
numbers: Gains (GPT-4-0613): CoT on ReClor +4.35%; CoT-SC on ReClor +6.52%; CoT-SC on RuleTaker +3.52%; ToT on ProofWriter +8%.
limits: Small subsets (ReClor 46 items, FOLIO 135, ProofWriter depth-5 100 items).
agent_relevance: A cheap way to supply derived consequences (contrapositives) as extra context before the model answers.

source: Lin, Le Bras, Richardson, Sabharwal, Poovendran, Clark, Choi (2025) ZebraLogic: On the Scaling Limits of LLMs for Logical Reasoning (ICML)
finding: Logic-grid puzzles (CSPs) with controllable size. Accuracy collapses as the search space grows (the 'curse of complexity'), even for reasoning models.
numbers: Overall puzzle accuracy: o1-full 81.0, DeepSeek-R1 78.7, o1-preview 71.4, o1-mini 59.7, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 36.2, Llama-3.1-405B 32.6, GPT-4o 31.7. X-Large puzzles (search space >10^9): o1-full 42.5, R1 28.5, o1-preview 17.0, o1-mini 12.0, GPT-4o 0.0.
limits: Model-to-row mapping read from PDF text; o1-preview 17.0 on X-Large and 71.4/59.7 for o1-preview/o1-mini are confirmed in the running text.
agent_relevance: Reasoning models help but still fail at large search. Give large constraint problems to Z3, not to the model.

source: Lin et al. (2025) ZebraLogic: repeated sampling and oracle selection
finding: Best-of-N with an oracle selector lifts GPT-4o a lot; without the oracle, sampling alone does not close the gap. Extra test-time compute has diminishing returns on big search spaces.
numbers: GPT-4o with BoN-Oracle at N=128 is far above N=1 (paper compares it with o1-preview's 88.2% on Medium puzzles); o1 models generate nearly 10 times more hidden reasoning tokens than non-reasoning models.
limits: Oracle selection is not available in practice. Exact BoN numbers were read from a figure description, not a table.
agent_relevance: The gap between oracle and real selection is the value of a checker. A solver is exactly that selector (G5).

source: Jiang, Welleck, Zhou et al. (2023) Draft, Sketch, and Prove: Guiding Formal Theorem Provers with Informal Proofs (ICLR)
finding: An LLM drafts an informal proof, turns it into a formal sketch with gaps, and a prover (Isabelle, Sledgehammer) fills the gaps. A prover loop inside an LLM pipeline.
numbers: miniF2F-test success rate raised from 20.9% to 39.3% over the earlier baseline (abstract); 38.9% with LM-generated informal proofs. Thor plus expert iteration 35.2% on the same test set.
limits: Math theorem proving in Isabelle, not natural-language logic. Table alignment in the PDF text was unreliable; only abstract-level numbers are used.
agent_relevance: A working 'model proposes, formal checker disposes' loop; a formal proof cannot be faked by fluent text.

source: Wu, Jiang, Li, Rabe, Staats, Jamnik, Szegedy (2022) Autoformalization with Large Language Models (NeurIPS)
finding: Codex translates competition math from English into Isabelle/HOL. A quarter of problems translate perfectly. Training a prover on the formalized statements improved it.
numbers: 25.3% of competition problems translated perfectly; miniF2F proof rate raised from 29.6% to 35.2% after two expert iterations. Most failures come from misaligned informal and formal definitions.
limits: Math domain, Isabelle; translation correctness was judged by hand on a sample.
agent_relevance: Translation errors are the main cost; plan an independent check of the formalization.
